headline: Former staff of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind told the New York City Council that the biggest tech companies are building technology they do not know how to control.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a public hearing with named witnesses and officials, confirmed by AP and Fortune; the warnings are the witnesses' own views.
importance_line: New Yorkers could get local rules such as outside approval of AI systems, because the federal government has been passive, but the proposals are not law and the extinction warning is Coxon's own forecast.
summary: The Associated Press reports that former Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind staff told the New York City Council on Monday 5 Oct of a reckless culture at their firms, and that the biggest tech companies are racing to build technology they do not know how to control. Jacob Coxon, a former Anthropic engineer whose testimony Reuters previewed on 4 Oct, said he thinks humanity is, on the current path, more likely than not to lose control of AI, which could end in human extinction, while company representatives said safety is their focus.
notes: AP's own page returned 403; text read from AP's wire story as carried by the Times Union (fuller, later version) and GazetteXtra, and cross-checked with Fortune's account of the same hearing. Pool flags a follow-up of 1005:C13-10 (Reuters 4 Oct, citing Bloomberg News, that Coxon would testify; pool only, not in the 5 Oct edition); the hearing itself was held on 5 Oct, so freshness is NEW. The summary carries the new facts: what was said at the hearing.
